_note: The first-person arms from KINEMATION's FPS Animation Ultimate (docs/PLAN_FIRST_PERSON_ARMS.md), a paid pack: its files are made by `npm run paid` (tools/import-fparms.ts) into models/paid/arms/, never in git, shipped only with the game server. `general` are the clips every gun shares; `packGuns` are the pack's guns whose holds we use, each with its arms clips (A_FP_) and its gun's own clips (A_W_, which move the pack gun's magazine, bolt and charging handle), and the pack gun's model, read for its measurements and drawn only by the tools; `guns` maps our guns to them. The owner's order (2026-09-27): USSO and BOOG first, made right and shipped, then the rest. Ours: which pack gun stands in for which of ours is chosen on pictures at the owner's view.
_camera: Where the pack's camera sits in its rig, metres, the rig facing +z: its FPSPlayer prefab's Camera (field of view 80, near 0.01) at 0.012, 1.654, 0.06, 9 cm over the head bone. fprig.ts puts it on our eye, so the arms' shoulders stay where the pack made them, just out of the picture; the gun goes where our view puts it and both hands reach it (KINEMATION's own rig: the gun on its weapon bone, the hands on it by IK). Hung off our gun instead, the arms' shoulders and sleeves came into the view and filled a third of it.
_fov: The gun camera's vertical field of view at the hip while these arms hold the gun: the pack's own camera's (its FPSPlayer prefab, field of view 80), which its holds are made to be seen at. Ours at the default setting is 92, and the arms' forearms and the gun's back end, a few centimetres from the eye, filled the bottom of the view. Aimed, the sight picture is every gun's own (main.ts gunFov).
_adsShoulder: Metres both shoulders go back in the sights, on top of the pack gun's own clavicle offset (its settings asset): our sights bring the gun to the eye nearer than KINEMATION's player does (it stops short by the gun's aim point offset, 10 to 12 cm), and with the shoulder where the hold put it the USSO's right wrist bent 109 degrees aimed and its left 70 (tools/e2e.ts, the pack's wristBend).
_sprint: The pack's sprint on the gun (fprig.ts locomotion): its swing, 51 degrees across the body, comes in over `easeIn` s while sprinting and goes over `easeOut` s the moment you fire, aim or reload, and comes back `fireHold` s after the last shot. SpeedKills sprints whenever you move forward, firing included, and with the sprint on by speed alone the owner fired from a gun swung across the body, the tracers nowhere near the crosshair (2026-09-27, the live server). In the sights none of the pack's walk or sprint is kept. `swing` is how much of the pack's sprint (its tactical carry, the gun swung across the chest and rolled on its side) is used: none. SpeedKills sprints whenever you move, and with it on the owner saw the gun "crossed and inverted" the whole time he moved (2026-09-27); the run keeps the ready hold, the walk's bob carried on at a run.
_reload: The reload with the bought arms, the owner's (2026-09-27): "point a finger at it while it phases out and in for a reload and then smack the charging handle ... same with the sniper ... a nice combo of the two". Shares of the reload: the left hand leaves the gun over `point` and points at the magazine, its index finger out and its tip `gap` m off the magazine's left face, the hand `reach` m back from the tip along `aim` (in the gun's frame: right, up, ahead), while the gun turns its underside toward you (gunfeel.json reload.twist); the magazine phases out over `phaseOut` and a new one in over `phaseIn`, staying in the gun, and seats at `seat`; then over `rack` the pack's own hands work the gun: each pack gun's `rack` names the clip and the share of it where they do (measured off its gun clip: the MPS5's empty reload slaps its handle forward at 0.69, the L96X's fire clip works its bolt over 0.30 to 0.48), and the hands go back to the hold. It had been the pack's whole reload, the magazine carried out of the gun to the belt and back, its phase out of sight. `twist` turns the gun while the hand points (radians, and metres before the view's scale), smaller than gunfeel.json's own: at that one the gun filled the middle of the screen and the pointing hand came up to the eye. A pack gun's own `twist` replaces it: the USSO's magazine sits low, and at the shared one its pointing hand was below the screen's edge. Which face of the magazine the finger comes at is `face` (in the gun's frame; -1 on x its left face, -1 on y its bottom), `aim` the way it points, and a pack gun's own `point` replaces the three: the BOOG's magazine is a thin plate low on the gun's left side, and pointed at from its left the hand sat between the eye and it (2026-09-27, a picture with the magazine tinted red), so its finger comes up at its bottom, the gun pitched and rolled more to show it. The pointing arm's elbow bends toward `elbow` from its shoulder (in the view: right, up, toward you), hanging down: bent the way the hold had it, the USSO's point, 22 cm from the shoulder, folded the arm so tight that on the way its elbow passed 9 cm in front of the eye and the sleeve filled the view for a tenth of the reload (measured bone by bone, 2026-09-27). The hand points along the line from its shoulder to the fingertip, `bend` of the way toward `aim` (along `aim` alone the wrist bent 107 to 126 degrees), at `at` of the magazine's height from its bottom (its middle, up a pistol grip, is hidden by the other hand).
_swap: On a swap or holster the arms drop out of the picture as the gun phases out, and come back up to take the next one as it phases in (the owner: "the guns fly in and out but the arms stay in a weird position"): at the phase's bottom the whole rig is `drop` m lower, `back` m nearer and pitched `pitch` radians down, about the eye.
_guns: Which pack gun stands in for which of ours, chosen on pictures at the owner's view: the USSO's is the MPS5, a compact SMG held by its handguard, its charging handle worked from empty; the Striker-V, the first tried, holds its long magazine as a grip, 22 cm under where the USSO's short one sits, and the hand could not be on both. BOOG's is the L96X, a bolt sniper that works its bolt after every shot.
